## SECURITIES AND FUTURES COMMISSION

12th Floor, Edinburgh Tower, The Landmark, 15 Queen's Road Central, Hong Kong

## Securities and Futures Commission Investment Products Department

General Circular to persons registered with the SFC whose business involves the discretionary management of collective investment schemes (GC01/01-232/IP/6706)

Subject:

Provisions  in  the  Fund  Manager  Code  of  Conduct  that  may  be waived for Professional Investors

## Background

1. The revised Code of Conduct for Persons Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission  ('Code  of  Conduct')  was  issued  in  April  2001.  The  revised  Code  of Conduct has introduced a concept of Professional Investors. A registered person will not  be  required  to  fulfil  certain  requirements  of  the  Code  of  Conduct  in  respect  of relevant  products  or  markets  for  which  a  client  may  be  treated  as  a  Professional Investor.
2. The Commission has since received enquiries about whether the concept is applicable in the context of the Fund Manager Code of Conduct ('FMCC'). The Commission is pleased to clarify its position in this Circular.

## Professional Investors

3. The Commission is prepared to accept that, for the purpose of the FMCC, collective investment schemes ('CIS') may be treated as Professional Investors if the registered person  has  provided  a  written  explanation  to  them 1 explaining  the risks  and consequences of being treated as a Professional Investor, in particular, the information that  will  not  be  provided,  and  has  not  received  any  objection  on  behalf  of  the  CIS. This written explanation should also inform them that they have a right to withdraw from  being  treated  as  a  Professional  Investor  whether  in  respect  of  all  products  or markets or any part thereof.
4. CIS in the context of FMCC include unit trusts and mutual funds (whether authorised or unauthorised), pension and provident funds.

1 This refers to, where appropriate, the trustee, the board of directors, the management company or any other legal entities that enters into a client agreement with the registered person on behalf of the CIS.

## Provisions  in  the  Fund  Manager  Code  of  Conduct  that  may  be  waived  for Professional Investors

page 2

## Provisions that may be waived for Professional Investors

5. The following provisions in the FMCC may be waived for Professional Investors:
2. (a) Providing Information About the Firm (paragraph 6.1(a))
- the  need  to  provide  clients  with  adequate  information  about  the  firm including its business address, relevant conditions or restrictions under which its business is conducted, and the identity and status of persons acting on its behalf with whom the client may have contact;
4. (b) Account Opening Procedures / Information About Clients (paragraph 6.3(a)(ii))
- the need to establish a client's financial situation, investment experience, and investment objectives; and
6. (c) Reporting: Periodic Statements (paragraph 6.5)
- the need to provide each client with regular statements of account.
6. For  the  avoidance  of  doubt,  there  are  no  waivers  from  compliance  with  the  other requirements  of  the  FMCC  when  dealing  with  Professional  Investors.  In  particular, the requirement under paragraph 6.4.1 for the fund manager to ensure that a written agreement  (Client  Agreement)  is  entered  into  with  a  client  before  any  services  are provided to or transactions  made on behalf  of  that  client,  is  not  waived  for  CIS  as Professional  Investors.  Nevertheless,  as  stated  in  paragraph  6.4.2,  where  a  fund manager  is  providing  services  to  a  CIS,  a  written  management  agreement  in accordance with the rules of the CIS may be regarded as a Client Agreement.

## Revision of FMCC

7. The Commission intends to revise the FMCC in due course to update the regulatory requirements and bring its provisions in line with those of the Code of Conduct where appropriate. The market will be consulted as and when the review takes place.
8. In the meantime, please contact the Investment Products Department at 2840 9259 for enquiries.
